notes: Mission order said 1 spec dispatch and at most 2 plan dispatches; the conductor cap allows up to 4 per gate. The spec gate used 4 (round 1 carried a Critical toolchain defect); the plan gate used 3 (round 1 carried a real behavioral defect, round 2 a regression in an empty catalog, round 3 BLESSED). No round 5/4 was attempted.

The round-3 expert could not reproduce the aggregate hash f4c2ab08 with its own hashing but verified each file; our scripts/bless-hash.sh reproduced f4c2ab08 before the C1-C5 condition edits and a2f54abe after them.

Final latch design (implementation + e_opus-approved): the security book is carried across dead-listener eviction; protected_seen is committed only by spawn before either transport serves or by a winning register_plan_takeover under the plan lock; failed/cancelled first starts never commit; a stopped route never clears it. The earlier 'eviction drops the latch' residual note is superseded.

Dependency reading: 'no new dependencies' means no new package in the workspace or Cargo.lock. sha2 and noyalib join the crate dependency list; percent-encoding moves from dev-dependencies to dependencies. Cargo.lock changes only the camel-component-mcp dependency entry.
The latch is not the ADR-0061 Rule 8 bind-presence gate: it keys on registered route plans and governs the plan-less Skills catalog only.

Plan conditions carried into tasks.md: bound the file read with take(limit+1); skill_limits_are_inclusive_at_512_files_and_16_mib; skills_latch_ignores_refused_duplicate_plan; catalog_first_page_is_valid_on_an_empty_catalog. The final implementation replaced the register-time latch with commit-in-spawn/atomic-takeover during the holistic review.
